messages:
maria: Heads-up — security report filed: possible tampering during ACME renewal path for cert-provisioner in ap-south. Not confirmed, but logs show unexpected signer identity. :eyes:
jonathan: saw the ticket, pulling logs now. do we have KMS unwrap events around 2024-05-18T03:10Z?
sec-rotator-bot: ALERT: cert-rotator detected mismatch between issuer fingerprint and expected provenance for service=cert-provisioner-ap-south (id=rotator-43). Auto-rolled a shadow cert for canary.
kai: cc @samir-oncall — did we recently change the keystore IAM role for the rotator? there was an RBAC tweak last week for cross-region access.
olivia: checking audit logs now — I see a GetPublicKey + Decrypt attempt from principal:svc:rotator-ap-south:ephemeral-role-2024-05-18T02:58Z, followed by an external-agent call pattern that looks like the ACME webhook.
maria: if ephemeral-role did an unwrap, need to confirm which KMS key was used and which iam binding allowed it. can someone grep for keyId in the decrypt events?
jonathan: quick query (gcp-style) I ran: ```gcloud logging read 'resource.type=\"kms_key\" AND protoPayload.methodName=\"Decrypt\" AND timestamp>=\"2024-05-18T02:45:00Z\"' --limit 50 | jq '.[] | {time: .timestamp, principal: .protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail, key: .resource.labels.key_id}'``` returns 3 entries. two are expected (rotator service account), one shows principalEmail=\"svc-external-automation@partner[.]example\" — unfamiliar.
kai: that external principal is worrying. did we delegate any ACME choreography to partner accounts? I thought we used internal webhook only.
olivia: no delegations in RBAC policies for that key in IAM history. but there is a short-lived binding created by iam-audit service at 2024-05-17T23:59Z with note "temp-provision". need to track who created that.
maria: action items: 1) block the ephemeral role from unwrap on the KMS key (temp deny) 2) rotate affected certs to the shadow certs from bot so clients don't see mismatch 3) run a provenance sweep for other keys used in ACME flows 4) open an incident if we confirm external principal used it. assigning jonathan and kai.
samir-oncall: oncall here, I'll take incident lead if we escalate. start a P1 if we see external issuer signed production certs.
jonathan: ok I'm running a targeted rotate for cert-provisioner-ap-south now: `./tools/rotator rotate --service cert-provisioner-ap-south --use-shadow` — will post results.
jonathan: rotate finished, new cert issued from internal CA, canary traffic healthy. cert chain validated. no production CSR observed yet signed by external principal.
maria: good. still need forensics on that temp-provision binding. olivia, can you pull the audit trail for iam:bindRole events between 2024-05-17T22:00Z and 2024-05-18T03:00Z and capture requestor metadata?
olivia: pulling now — looks like request came from terraform-runner@infra-cicd with commit id a1b2c3. pinging infra-cicd team to confirm whether that was an intended change.
kai: if terraform-runner created a short-lived binding, check pipeline logs & secret scopes. could be a leaked token or misconfigured pipeline step.
maria: also add KMS access logs to long-term audit retention for this key (48h->30d) until we close investigation. we need all decrypt/unwrap/attest calls.
jonathan: quick mitigation checklist: revoke temp binding, add deny entry for external principals, rotate certs (done), bump audit retention, start CI pipeline token rotation, open infra ticket to root-cause terraform change.
maria: flagged for vuln-triage board. if infra confirms terraform change intentional, we treat as process gap, otherwise treat as compromise.
samir-oncall: I've informed legal & CS (prepped template) in case customer impact surfaces. notify me if we need to go public.
olivia: infra-cicd responded: pipeline triggered a one-off run by devops-jenkins during emergency maintenance; they claim no external principal was introduced. sharing run logs now.
kai: still odd — partner principal observed in KMS decrypt. may be downstream webhook from ACME provider that proxied request. can we map network flows from cert-provisioner to outside endpoints around that window?
jonathan: pulling egress flow logs for the pod in that timeframe. command: `kubectl logs -n cert cert-provisioner-abc | grep \"ACME hook\" -A5` and `gcp logging read 'resource.type=\"k8s_container\" AND jsonPayload.connection.dest_ip' --limit 100`
maria: thanks. we'll hold on escalation until jonathan has flow evidence or infra confirms pipeline. keep this thread updated. good job on rotate & canary. :thumbsup:
jonathan: flow logs show outbound to 35.200.12.9:443 which resolves to acme-provider.example-cdn.net and user-agent \"acme-client/2.1\" — matches expected provider. still investigating the external principal in KMS logs.
maria: ok, next steps: 24h full audit, RBAC deny in place, extended retention, pipeline token rotation, and incident playbook prepared. If anyone spots additional anomalies, add to this thread.
sec-rotator-bot: NOTE: shadow certs will be promoted to primary at 2024-05-18T06:00Z unless a rollback command is posted.
samir-oncall: acknowledged. I'll be watching through 06:00Z.
